Hi Priyom —

Thanks again for the private deployment walkthrough yesterday. As we start legal and security review, our InfoSec team asked for a short answers doc that we can attach to our DPA submission. Key items we need clarified:

1) Key ownership and custody: we want to use customer-managed keys (BYOK) in our cloud KMS for the on-prem/VPC deployment. Can you confirm whether Redwood ever has the ability to decrypt customer data (model inputs / outputs / logs) when customer-managed keys are in use?

2) Operator access: what specific operator actions (maintenance, migrations, crash debugging) could result in Redwood staff having access to plaintext? Is there an enforced breakglass workflow with approvals and audit trail?

3) Subprocessors: please provide a concise list of subprocessors that would touch telemetry, logging, or any unencrypted artifacts in a private deployment.

4) Cross-border transfers & subpoenas: what is the legal process if Redwood receives a lawful request for data when customer keys are used?

5) Telemetry & metrics: we need to understand the minimal telemetry that Redwood requires for health checks and whether that telemetry can be filtered to remove PII or model content.

If you can answer these at a high level in-line, and attach any DPA redline template you recommend, that would be ideal — we will then loop in procurement. We are targeting a compliance decision by next Thursday.

Best,

Alyssa Park
Head of Security
Trias HealthTech

Alyssa —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers below; attaching a KMS/access matrix and a draft DPA redline for procurement. Happy to run through details on a call.

1) Key ownership and decrypt capability
- If Trias configures a customer-managed KMS (BYOK) and we are not escrow holders, Redwood does not have persistent ability to decrypt customer model I/O or logs.
- There are two limited exceptions where an operator action could result in temporary decryption: emergency breakglass for live debugging, and customer-authorized key handoff for data migration. Both are governed by the breakglass protocol described below.

2) Operator access / breakglass workflow
- Operator role is strictly JIT (just-in-time) with time-boxed access, multi-person approval (2-of-3 on-call + engineering manager), and live recorded session (terminal and KMS unwrap logs).
- All breakglass requests generate an immutable audit bundle (who/why/nonce/commands) and require documented customer approval unless the customer has explicitly pre-authorized a specific runbook in the DPA annex.
- We propose adding a contract addendum that requires Redwood to produce the audit bundle within 24 hours of request.

3) Subprocessors
- For private deployments in customer VPCs / private on-prem, the core Redwood operators and support teams are the primary internal agents. External subprocessors that may be involved for provisioning or monitoring are:
  * CloudOps Partner LLC (provisioning automation) — no access to keys or plaintext
  * DataMetrics Ltd (aggregated health telemetry only) — receives only anonymized metrics unless customer opts in
  * SecLog Solutions (log ingestion/rotation; sees metadata and non-sensitive operational logs)
- I have included a spreadsheet with the subprocessors, role, and whether they receive any encrypted blobs.

4) Cross-border transfers & lawful requests
- When customer keys are BYOK and Redwood does not hold key material, Redwood cannot produce plaintext to comply with a lawful request. We will provide metadata and encrypted blobs and the exact request record; legal process for a compelled disclosure would require either customer cooperation (to decrypt) or that Redwood maintain a court order for key escrow release only under narrowly defined statutes (we don't hold escrow unless contractually agreed).

5) Telemetry & metrics
- Minimum telemetry: process health, pod-level CPU/memory, request latency percentiles, error rates, and aggregated token throughput.
- Model inputs/outputs and raw logs can be disabled in telemetry or redacted at the ingestion point; we can provide a filtered telemetry feed that drops model content and PII.

Next steps:
- Attached: redwood_privdep_kms_matrix.xlsx and a DPA redline (redwood_dpa_redline_20270518.pdf).
- Suggested follow-up: 30-min compliance sync on Wed afternoon. I can coordinate.

Regards,

Priyom Das

Alyssa / team — quick technical addendum from infra: 

- KMS handshake model: Redwood supports two modes for private deploys:
  1) Customer-hosted KMS (recommended): customer retains keying material; Redwood requests key unwrap operations via a minimal API where only a transient unwrapping token is returned; tokens expire in seconds and are not persisted.
  2) Escrowed KMS (only if contractually agreed): we can hold encrypted key shares in an HSM behind legal controls; these shares require multi-sig release and are audited.

- Operator debugging: we avoid moving plaintext outside the customer's environment. When a debug session requires data-level visibility, we prefer a collaborative session where a customer engineer temporarily grants decryption, or we run a securely provisioned ephemeral worker inside the customer's VPC with customer keys and a scoped session.

- Telemetry sanitization points: we can provide a filter plugin that runs on the agent side (customer-managed) to strip prompts/outputs before any outbound telemetry pipeline.

- Cryptographic proofs: if helpful, we can provide a short technical appendix showing KMS unwrap flow and audit log hashing (SHA-256 chain) for the audit bundles.

-Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Alyssa / team —

Attached is a concise DPA appendix paragraph plus a redline we recommend for your procurement team. I also flagged each subprocessor row in the matrix with: 
  - "no-plaintext": vendor never sees plaintext or decrypted model IO
  - "anonymized-metrics": vendor receives only aggregated/anonymized telemetry
  - "ops-metadata": vendor receives operational logs without user content

Key contract points I recommend adding to the SOW/DPA:
1) Breakglass SLA: Redwood will provide the breakglass audit bundle within 8 business hours of request and delivery of the bundle will be via secure transfer; if Redwood needs additional time (rare), we will provide status updates every 2 hours.
2) Escrow policy: Redwood will not hold customer key material unless an escrow addendum is signed; escrow releases require court order and two Redwood exec approvals + customer-designated approver.
3) On-prem physical access: any on-site vendor action requires customer-scheduled access windows and badge logs; subcontractor personnel will be named in an appendix before any on-site work.

One-paragraph DPA blurb you can paste: 
"Redwood Inference acknowledges that where a customer supplies and controls cryptographic keys for a private deployment, Redwood will not possess or retain any independent ability to decrypt customer data (including model inputs, outputs, and logs) except where the customer has provided explicit, documented authorization for a specific recovery or debugging activity. Any such authorized activity will follow the contractual breakglass workflow and be recorded in an immutable audit bundle delivered to the customer within the SLA defined in this agreement."
